batch_node.name: fedramp_20x_ksi findings-genericom-alb-port80 v0.1.0
batch_node.description: Seeds an unencrypted-HTTP-listener finding against the prod-web-alb itself: nmap detects port 80/tcp open serving HTTP. In reality the listener is just a 301 redirect to https://, but the violation is recorded here so the exception process can be exercised against it. Backed by mocked nmap scanner_output evidence.

entity.name: Unencrypted HTTP listener on ALB port 80

node.name: Unencrypted HTTP listener on ALB port 80
node.summary: prod-web-alb is accepting plaintext HTTP on port 80 alongside its HTTPS listener.
node.description:
External nmap scanning confirms that prod-web-alb has an open TCP/80 listener serving HTTP, in addition to its HTTPS listener on TCP/443. Under FedRAMP 20x SC controls, public-facing endpoints must not accept unencrypted HTTP traffic — even briefly — because the request line, Host header, cookies, and any query-string parameters traverse the public internet in cleartext before any redirect can take effect.

Operator note: in this deployment the port 80 listener is configured to issue an HTTP 301 redirect to the matching `https://` URL on the same host and serves no application content. The redirect does not retroactively encrypt the inbound request that triggered it — clients that send credentials or session cookies over HTTP have already leaked them by the time the 301 response is returned. A pure-redirect listener is therefore a common operational convenience but still represents a violation of the encryption-in-transit control as written. The intended resolution path is either (a) remove the port 80 listener entirely and rely on HSTS-preloaded clients, or (b) record an exception documenting the redirect-only behavior and the compensating controls (HSTS, no application routes mounted on :80).

node.name: nmap detects HTTP on prod-web-alb:80
node.description:
Automated check: `nmap -sV -p 80 --script=http-title,http-methods,http-headers prod-web-alb.genericom.com`

The scan confirms that TCP/80 is open on the ALB, that the listener speaks HTTP/1.1, and captures the response headers and status line. The `http-title` and `http-headers` NSE scripts are the canonical scripts for fingerprinting an HTTP listener — `-sV` performs the version probe (which is what flags the service as `http` rather than just `tcp/open`), and the two scripts add the `Server` banner, response headers, and any HTML `<title>` element to the report.

Last run: 2026-05-06 09:12:44 UTC. Result: FAIL (port 80/tcp open, serving HTTP).

--- what we are seeing ---

PORT 80/tcp open
  └── the ALB has an active listener on TCP/80 and accepts connections
      from the public internet. This alone is the violation: SC-8 / SC-13
      require that data-in-transit on public-facing endpoints be
      cryptographically protected, and an open :80 listener accepts the
      cleartext request before any application-layer redirect can run.

SERVICE http, VERSION `awselb/2.0`
  └── the `-sV` version probe negotiated HTTP/1.1 successfully and
      identified the listener as the AWS ELB httpd, confirming this is
      a real HTTP responder and not a stray TCP service masquerading
      on port 80.

http-headers: `Location: https://prod-web-alb.genericom.com/` + http-title `301 Moved Permanently`
  └── the listener is configured as a redirect-only listener — every
      response is HTTP 301 to the https:// equivalent. This is the
      operational behavior the system owner is expected to document
      in the exception request: no application content is served on
      :80, only the redirect. The redirect is informative, not
      exculpatory — the violation is the open cleartext port itself.

Result: prod-web-alb is accepting plaintext HTTP on port 80. Listener responds with a 301 redirect to https, but the cleartext channel is open before the redirect is issued.
